title: AssemblyAI for Healthcare: the most accurate voice AI for clinical products
summary: Ambient scribes, healthcare voice agents, and clinical dictation run on AssemblyAI. Today we’re taking that accuracy further with an updated Medical Mode and a new Vet Mode in beta.
body_markdown:
## What’s new in Medical Mode


Medical Mode adds a correction pass tuned for clinical language on top of our speech-to-text models. It finds medical terms the model heard but spelled wrong, like drug names, procedures, and conditions, and fixes them using the context around them.


In our benchmarks, turning on Medical Mode, compared to a base AssemblyAI model, resulted in up to 13% fewer missed medical terms, with no rise in wrongly inserted terms. On Universal-2, Medical Mode cuts missed medical terms by 27%.


We ran five other speech-to-text services on the nine datasets in the four languages Medical Mode supports, with the same metrics, each in its medical-specific model or mode wherever the vendor offers one for the language: Soniox (stt-async-v6 and stt-rt-v6), ElevenLabs (Scribe v2 Medical for batch, Scribe v2 Realtime for streaming), Google Gemini 3.5 Transcribe (batch and Live), Deepgram (nova-3-medical where it accepts the language, nova-3 otherwise) and Speechmatics (Enhanced with the medical domain where supported).

Averaged over the nine pre-recorded sets, AssemblyAI with Medical Mode has the lowest error rate on all three measures: WER, overall medical-term misses and drug-name misses (see the chart above).


For streaming, error rate is only half the picture: a system also has to commit its words quickly. Speechmatics and Soniox have the lowest or near-lowest error rates, but at default settings they finalize words about 5 seconds behind the audio. Among the systems that finalize within about a second, AssemblyAI with Medical Mode has the lowest error on all three measures. Without Medical Mode, the same model is the fastest system in the benchmark at 0.63 seconds, with the same WER but more missed drug names, so you can trade drug-name accuracy for a faster time-to-final.

Unweighted mean error rate over the same nine medical datasets, streaming audio. The dashed lines are reading guides, not benchmark thresholds. Time-to-final is the 90th percentile on clips of 10 seconds and longer at each vendor’s default settings, measured on read English speech. “(medical)” marks a system run in its medical model or mode. Both AssemblyAI rows are Universal-3.6 Pro Realtime, with and without Medical Mode. Soniox, ElevenLabs, and Gemini offer no medical variant for streaming. Deepgram’s streaming medical model accepts English and German as pinned languages, so Spanish and French ran on its multi-language setting. ElevenLabs’ German results stitch partial transcripts and are less reliable than the rest, and Gemini Live returned short transcripts on two sets, so part of its error is dropped audio. No system received custom vocabulary or keyterms. All values: streaming averages over nine sets (lower is better)

Our latest models already handle most medical vocabulary well, so Medical Mode’s lift depends on your specific audio and your vocabulary. Run your files with and without it, score both on the terms that matter to your users, and keep Medical Mode on wherever it performs best. Developers already using Medical Mode with` domain: "medical-v1"` have received the update automatically, no changes needed.


[Read the full technical deep dive →](https://www.assemblyai.com/blog/assemblyai-for-healthcare-research)


**Where it runs:**


- **Pre-recorded:** Universal-3.5 Pro and Universal-2
- **Streaming:** Universal-3.6 Pro Realtime, Universal-3.5 Pro Realtime, and Universal-Streaming English and Multilingual
- **Languages:** English, Spanish, German, and French
- **Pricing:** $0.15/hr add-on


```text
import requests


response = requests.post(
"https://api.assemblyai.com/v2/transcript",
headers={"authorization": "YOUR_API_KEY"},
json={
"audio_url": "https://example.com/clinical-visit.mp3",
"speech_models": ["universal-3-5-pro"],
"domain": "medical-v1",
},
)
print(response.json()["id"])
```
